chunks: One of our companions narrated from Jābir ibn Sadr, from Muʿādh ibn Muslim who said:

I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) while there was a man with him, and Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) told him, ‘The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Gentleness is propitious, and roughness is inauspicious.’

key_terms.الرِّفْقُ: Gentleness, kindness, or ease in conduct
key_terms.الْخِرْقُ: Roughness, coarseness, or harshness of character

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Rifq yumn wa al-khirq shoom' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in *Kitab al-Zuhd* by Husayn ibn Sa'id al-Ahwazi, encapsulates the Prophetic principle that *al-riqq* (gentleness/tact) invites divine blessing (*yumn*), whereas *al-khirq* (roughness/coarseness) signals misfortune. In Shia ethical tradition, this serves as a foundational metric for evaluating interpersonal conduct, linking spiritual tranquility directly to the quality of one's demeanor. It reinforces the idea that moral refinement is not merely social etiquette but a conduit for divine favor.
